title: Day 2: Write the policy first
caption:
Write your cancellation policy before the first no-show, not after.

A policy written in a hurry after a missed session reads like a grudge. Written ahead of time, it is just how you work.

Three things worth deciding up front: until when clients can cancel or reschedule, what happens to their payment if they cancel late, and what a no-show means.

In Schedulign each event has its own cancellation settings. You decide whether clients can cancel or reschedule online and until when, and your written policy shows as a link on the booking page before they book.

Try it free during early access. Link in bio: schedulign.com

caption:

A booking page answers all of it once. The client sees your open times in their own time zone, picks one, answers your questions and gets a confirmation email with a calendar invite and a private link to reschedule or cancel. You get the booking, already confirmed.

title: Day 4: How a client books
caption:
How a client books you, start to finish.

1. They open your link and pick an event.
2. They pick a day on the calendar and a time from the list.
3. They enter their details and answer your questions.
4. They book, and the confirmation arrives by email.

No account to create and no password to forget. Swipe through the real screens.

Create your booking page at schedulign.com (link in bio). Free during early access.

title: Day 5: Why Schedulign
caption:
Why I am building Schedulign.

Sam here, the founder. I kept seeing the same setup: bookings in a message thread, a waitlist in a group chat, payments across a few apps, and a spreadsheet trying to hold it together.

Schedulign puts that on one page. Clients book and pay without an account, your rules decide what they can change, and people who want a time that is taken can ask to hear when one opens.

It is in early access now, and the people using it shape what gets built next. If you sell your time, I would like you to try it.

Try it free during early access. Link in bio: schedulign.com

title: Day 6: Mobile pros: the client gives the address
caption:
Mobile detailer? Let the client tell you where the car is.

When you go to the client, the address is part of the booking. An event can ask the client for their own address at booking, with room for access details like a gate code or where to park.

Add buffers before and after each booking so drive time never gets booked over.

The same event settings work for anyone who travels: mobile groomers, trainers who come to the house, photographers on location.

Early access is open and every plan is $0 while it runs. Link in bio: schedulign.com

title: Day 8: No client accounts
caption:
Your clients never make an account. Ever.

Every booking comes with one private link in the confirmation email. From it, a client can reschedule or cancel inside the windows you set, add the session to their calendar, and see their booking.

Lost the email? The Find my bookings page sends a link to every upcoming booking for that address.

Fewer passwords for them, fewer "how do I log in" messages for you.

caption:

Build the gap in. Time to reset a room, write notes, drive across town, or eat something.

In Schedulign every event can keep minutes free before and after each booking, and cap how many bookings it takes in a day, a week or a month. The booking page only offers what fits.

Early access is open and every plan is $0 while it runs. Link in bio: schedulign.com

title: Day 10: Openings alerts
caption:
Before: "Anything open Thursday?" After: they get an email when something opens.

When your week is full, clients can ask to hear about new openings, from a bell under your calendar. They can limit it to certain dates and times, and choose how long to keep hearing.

When a time opens inside their window, they get an email. If a day is fully booked, they can join that day's waitlist, and the first person in line gets the freed time held for them for two hours.

You decide per event whether alerts go out automatically or only when you send them.

Create your booking page at schedulign.com (link in bio). Free during early access.

The client picks the length and group size, and the total updates before they book. Their participants' names come with the booking.

title: Day 15: Online or offline payment
caption:
Paid online or offline. You choose, per event.

Take card payments through your own Stripe account, or keep being paid the way you already are, by cash, bank transfer or a payment app, with your payment instructions shown at booking. One event can take cards and the next can be paid offline.

Card payments carry Stripe's standard processing fee. Schedulign adds nothing on top.

Early access is open and every plan is $0 while it runs. Link in bio: schedulign.com

Clients see it before they pick: peak times are shaded on the booking page with their price and a label, so nobody meets a surprise total at the end.

You can also let clients request a time you have not listed, so a good fit is never turned away by the calendar.
